pages.text:
Wells Fargo
Siddhesh Bandgar, Final Year BTech 2022
Wells Fargo visited our campus in August 2021 to hire final year students for the
role of Program Associate B.
Branches allowed were: Computer Engineering , Information Technology,
Electronics, Telecommunication, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering,
Mechanical Engineering.
They did not mention any pointer criteria in their JD, shortlisting was done by their
own criteria.
Whole process was conducted virtually due to China.
Total 4 rounds were conducted overall.
1. Online test
2. Technical Round 1
3. Technical + Managerial  Round
4. HR Round
Round 1 (Online Test):
This was an AMCAT test hosted on SHL platform (Aspiring Minds platform). There
was no negative marking, and we cannot move backwards once a question is
submitted (Except the coding section). There were 3 sections:
1

1. Verbal Ability (12 MCQs in 15 mins): Had standard English questions asked
in any AMCAT test like correct the sentence, fill up with the appropriate word,
arrange the jumbled parts of a sentence and a passage at the end (passage
consisted of 4 questions).
2. Business Aptitude (15 MCQs in 25mins): Had several case studies. Tables
or graphs were given for each of them. The questions were to test how well
you analyze and understand the given data. Speed was key here.
3. Coding (2 questions in 60mins): Everybody got 2 questions from a larger
pool of questions
a. An online multiplayer game assigns n players  a random number when they
log into the game. For every round, we take the player with the maximum
and minimum number assigned. The difference between their values is the
cost of each round. The player with maximum value is removed and the
player with minimum value is reassigned with the value of the cost
(difference between maximum and minimum value) of that particular round.
If the two players have the same value,  the one who logs in first is
considered. We have to print the sum of the costs of all the rounds. As the
sum can be very large, print sum%1000000007.
Input contains the n: number of players and
an array of size n, containing the values assigned to each player in the order
of time as they log into the game.
2

b. (This question was a little bit confusing, I could not figure out what they
actually wanted)There are N devices that are in a network, having id’s
between 1 to n, connected with a physical link (wire). There is a cost
associated with each connection. The administrator while upgrading the
network changes a few links to wireless medium. Consequently the cost of
those links also changed.
Input consists of n: the number of devices on the network.
Next it contains T , a nxn matrix having the cost of connection between i and
j as T[i][j] , 1<=i<=n & 1<=j<=n. If there is no direct connection between i & j,
then T[i][j] is INT_MAX (or some large value)
Next it contains m: the number of links upgraded to wireless medium.
Next m lines contained 3 integers,
device _1_id   device_2_id   cost of the wireless link between them
We have to print m integers, the minimum cost to connect the upgraded
links.
I solved most of the questions from the verbal ability and business aptitude section.
In the coding part, I solved the 1st question and passed 20/21 test cases. In the
second question, I applied some brute force logic and cleared only 3/11 test cases.
The verbal and aptitude sections are equally important to clear this round. 30
students cleared this round.
3

Round 2 (Technical Interview):
Interviewer asked me to introduce myself. He then asked to elaborate my
internship project. He asked questions from DSA, OOPS, DBMS, SQL as wells as OS:
1. What data structure will you use if your priority is searching the data
efficiently, similarly if priority is inserting the data efficiently? Why? What is
the time complexity of the searching and inserting in that data structure?
2. What are oops concepts?. Explain real life examples of all. I gave an example
of a car for abstraction. He asked a lot of counter questions on this example.
Explain advantages of the concepts from a developer perspective.  (Be really
thorough with oops concepts to answer these).
3. What is a thread?
4. What is multi tasking, multiprocessing and multiprogramming?
5. Difference between multitasking and multiprogramming.
6. Explain multitasking and multiprogramming in a windows machine.
7. What are cores in a cpu?
8. Difference between multiple cores and multiple cpus. Which is better?
9. Find the nth highest salary from a given employee table. He asked for various
different approaches. (Using subquery/ TOP keyword/ LIMIT keyword, etc)
10.What is dbms?
11.What data structure is used internally in a dbms to store the records?
12.What are B, B+ trees?
13.Explain different types of trees that you know. (AVL trees, Red-Black trees)
14.What is the difference between BST and Balanced trees?
15. Suppose there is a huge file containing huge lines of text. Every line is itself a
huge sentence. We have to find out how many lines in the file contain all the
26 characters (a-z). I started with a brute force approach of using a set data
structure. The interviewer helped optimize that solution. Still, he was
expecting a more optimized solution.
4

16.How will you multiply 2 very big numbers efficiently?
17.Explain merge sort.
(Actually more questions were asked but I remember only these😅). Interviewer
was providing hints wherever I was stuck. As the interview was already extended,
he told me to leave the meeting and said that he’ll convery his feedback to the hr.
Round 3 (Technical + Managerial Interview):
This round was a little different for me (I assumed this because most of my friends
were asked to solve one puzzle and to write the code of that puzzle. Depends on
the interviewer).
The interviewer was very friendly, he asked me if I had my lunch. Then he first
introduced himself and told me to do the same. He then asked me if I knew what
Wells Fargo is and what they do. I said  I have a basic idea and told whatever I
remembered from the ppt. Then for about 10-15 minutes he talked about Wells
Fargo, what they did, their origin, the technological advancements in the financial
sector, what they expected from us, and a lot of different things. I was listening
keenly and also asking a few questions in between. It was a very good conversation
kind of thing.
I had interned at Samsung R&D, Bangalore. So he asked that if they also offer a
PPO, then what would I choose? Never say that you’ll choose any other company,
even if it is google or microsoft.
He then asked me if I had to make a software that takes input the monthly
expenses of a whole family and then tells what to spend, what not to spend, where
to spend, what to buy with the current savings, etc, how would I do this? What all
parameters would I need? He asked a lot of questions on this question/case study.
He was not expecting any technical details of the system, just checking my thought
5

process. What all features I would add, how would I make this system efficient to
adapt to different families across India and so on. This went on for about 25-30
mins.
He then asked what technologies/programming languages I would like to work with
in future and what technologies would I wish were discarded/scraped in future.
The interviewer was quite satisfied with my answers. He asked me if I had any
questions for him. I asked a few questions and the interview ended.
Round 4 (HR Round):
This round happened after a long time after the 3rd round. It was a telephonic
round and was quite chill. HR asked me a few basic questions like: how was your
day, where are you from, are you willing to relocate, do you have any plans for
higher studies, etc.
She then asked if I was clear with the compensation details and the breakup. And
the interview ended.
The results were announced at around 8-9 in the evening, and a total of 7 students
were selected for a full time offer.
Out of the 7 selected students, some of them were not selected for the 3rd and the
4th interview rounds but still they got the offer. Apparently Wells Fargo has a points
based system for selecting candidates, so if your points from the online coding
round and 1st interview are good enough, you don’t need to give the rest of the
rounds. Pretty dope!
6

Some Tips to ace your interview:
1. Placements are very exhausting. Key here is patience and to stay motivated.
Don’t be sad because your friends are getting selected. Learn from them,
what they do better, learn from your own mistakes. Remember that a lot of
good companies visit our campus so always try your best but don’t get
demotivated if you are not selected in the first few companies.
2. Always have a smile throughout your interview, it creates a good impression.
3.
DO NOT LIE IN YOUR RESUME, they ask questions from it, so it is important
to know everything you’ve written in your resume.
4. Don’t forget to prepare yourself for behavioral questions. Sometimes, we
focus a lot on technical questions and completely ignore behavioral
questions.
5. Always read interview experiences from gfg before your interviews/test. They
give you a fair idea of what type of questions are asked in a particular
company and also you feel a little prepared.
6. Theory subjects like OS, DBMS, OOPS, CN and SQL are very very important.
Don’t ignore them at all.
All the best for your interviews!!
7
